title: Optimized intrusion detection using particle swarm optimization and neural networks in simulated and physical network environments
author: Ganesh, Deshmukh

steps.title: Create simulated network
steps.instruction: Design and build the desired network topology in Cisco Packet Tracer, defining all source and destination nodes as required.

steps.title: Capture simulated traffic
steps.instruction: Run the simulated network and use Wireshark to capture all packets exchanged between the nodes; export the capture file for later processing.

steps.title: Build physical network
steps.instruction: Assemble a real‑world network using routers, switches and PCs that mirrors the simulated topology, connecting all nodes accordingly.

steps.title: Capture physical traffic
steps.instruction: Operate the physical network and record packet flows with Wireshark, saving the capture files for dataset creation.

steps.title: Induce network intrusions
steps.instruction: Perform the four attack types on both simulated and physical networks: denial‑of‑service (label 1), probing (label 2), R2L (label 3), and U2R (label 4); capture the resulting traffic with Wireshark.

steps.title: Assemble datasets
steps.instruction: Combine the captured traffic from simulated, physical, and intrusion runs into a single dataset and merge it with standard benchmark datasets (NSL‑KDD, UNSW‑NB15, KDD Cup). Label each record with 0 = normal, 1 = DOS, 2 = probing, 3 = R2L, 4 = U2R.

steps.title: Select features with PSO
steps.instruction: Apply the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm to each dataset to perform feature selection, reducing the original 48 features to approximately 25 features.

steps.title: Train machine‑learning models
steps.instruction: Using the reduced‑feature datasets, train the following classifiers: Decision Tree (DT), K‑Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Adaboost, and Logistic Regression.

steps.title: Evaluate model performance
steps.instruction: For each trained model compute Predictability, Accuracy, NPV, F1‑Rank, Precision, Detection Rate, and False Positive Rate (FPR). Record the results:

substeps.instruction: PSO+DT – Predictability 98.8 %, Accuracy 75.2 %, NPV 99.5 %, F1‑Rank 81.7 %, Precision 98.5 %, Detection Rate 89.5 %, FPR 1.2 %
PSO+KNN – Predictability 99.6 %, Accuracy 88.4 %, NPV 99.8 %, F1‑Rank 92.1 %, Precision 99.5 %, Detection Rate 96.1 %, FPR 0.3 %
PSO+ANN – Predictability 99.7 %, Accuracy 90.2 %, NPV 99.8 %, F1‑Rank 94.1 %, Precision 99.77 %, Detection Rate 97.2 %, FPR 0.02 %
PSO+ANN – True Positive Rate 99.78 %, False Positive Rate 0.003 %

steps.title: Compare with existing IDS
steps.instruction: Contrast the above results with previously reported systems:

substeps.instruction: DT (Vu Viet Thang et al.) – Accuracy 98.2 %, FPR 0.0 %
Genetic Algorithm (Preeti & Kusum Deep) – Accuracy 96.4 %, FPR 0.05 %

steps.title: Document limitations and future work
steps.instruction: Note that the system is primarily effective within the monitored network, has limited detection of external/upstream attacks, and that PSO‑based feature selection may omit rare but relevant features; suggest expanding adaptability to dynamic networks and exploring alternative optimization techniques.
